topics.title: U.S. jobs report shows a stall
topics.summary: U.S. employers unexpectedly cut 23,000 jobs in July, while revised spring numbers were weaker than first reported. The report renewed debate about household finances and the economy's direction.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a jobs report surprises everyone, do you trust the national numbers more, or the hiring signs you see around town?

topics.title: Colombia swears in new president
topics.summary: Abelardo de la Espriella took office as Colombia's president in Cali, promising a tougher security approach and a break from the previous government's left-leaning policies.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a new leader holds the big ceremony outside the capital, is that practical politics, stagecraft, or a little of both?

topics.title: Kellogg speeds up cereal dye change
topics.summary: WK Kellogg says it will remove artificial colors from its U.S. cereals by the end of 2026, covering familiar brands like Froot Loops and Apple Jacks.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a bright cereal changes its colors but keeps the same taste, who at the breakfast table notices first?

topics.title: mRNA flu shot gets closer look
topics.summary: Moderna's mRNA-based flu vaccine has drawn federal review and adviser attention, showing how vaccine technology from the COVID era may keep moving into ordinary seasonal medicine.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would newer vaccine tech make you more interested in a flu shot, or would it mostly make you ask extra questions first?
